weather.label: Heat
weather.line: Good growing weather for your wheat.

detail.title: Heat and your crop
detail.what: Good growing weather for your wheat.
detail.why: Wheat is hurt most by days over 32 °C while it flowers and fills its grain (heading to grain filling). Each hot day then can cost a few percent of the harvest.
detail.how_to_check: Around midday, look at the leaf tips. Rolled, dull grey-green leaves mean heat stress.

weather.label: Soil water
weather.sub: Refill point 50%. Rain since last watering 3 mm
weather.line: Plenty of water in the roots. No need to water before your turn.
weather.source: FAO-56 water balance on NASA POWER weather and your watering log

detail.title: Water in the root zone
detail.what: Plenty of water in the roots. No need to water before your turn.
detail.why: Bezra counts the water your crop uses every day (from NASA weather), the rain and your waterings. Below 50% the plant closes its leaves and grows less.
detail.how_to_check: Push a finger or a stick 10 cm into the soil in the middle of the field. Dry and crumbly means the crop needs water; cool and sticky means it still has water.

detail.title: Humidity and leaf disease
detail.why: Yellow rust needs cool nights (7 to 18 °C) with dew or fog on the leaves.
detail.how_to_check: In the morning, look at the top leaves of 10 plants across the field. Yellow-orange powder in stripes that rubs off on your finger is yellow rust. Take a photo and send it to your engineer.

warnings.title: Your crop may run short of water
warnings.reason: Your turn of 9 Nov was missed. Water today if you can.
warnings.how_to_check: Push a finger or a stick 10 cm into the soil in the middle of the field. Dry and crumbly means the crop needs water; cool and sticky means it still has water.

warnings.title: The north-east corner looks weaker
warnings.reason: 16% less green than the rest of your field in the last 2 satellite images (about 0.21 feddan). Likely cause: water. You said the turn on 2026-11-09 was not done.
warnings.how_to_check: Walk to that part of the field. Compare leaf colour and plant height with the rest. Look for dry soil, insects, weeds or water standing.

plan.title: Fertilizer, second dose
plan.amount: About 75–85 kg of urea 46% per feddan (1.5 bags). For your 3 feddan: about 240 kg. Check the amount with your engineer.
plan.why: Put it the day before the water turn so the water carries it to the roots.
plan.source: Timing from MALR wheat guide; amount from your engineer

detail.title: Fertilizer, second dose

get.benefit: Feeds the crop when it grows fastest

detail.what: Put the fertilizer on Wednesday 18 Nov, the day before your water turn.
detail.how_to_do: Put it the day before the water turn. Your engineer sets the amount.
